title: National Recycling Rates, Plans and Targets
what_it_is: National Recycling Rates, Plans and Targets

sections.label: Waste and recycling questions
sections.summary: Questions ask about recyclable and industrial versus domestic waste proportions, recycling targets, lessons, and measures for glass, paper and textiles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) out of the 3.35 million tonnes of waste disposed of in 2025 (i) what is the estimated proportion that is recyclable and (ii) what is the proportion of industrial versus domestic waste; and (b) of the 52% recycling rate, what are the main categories of recycled waste and their corresponding proportions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether the Ministry has an ideal yearly national recycling rate target for 2026 to 2030; (b) what lessons have been learnt from how Singapore's waste and recycling profile has changed over the past decade; and (c) what updated measures are being considered to improve recycling rates for (i) glass (ii) paper and cardboard and (iii) textiles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) whether the Zero Waste Master Plan review will focus on reducing overall waste produced or circular economy outcomes rather than recycling rates, in view of the high contamination rates for recycling; and (b) whether the Ministry plans to implement nationwide clean-stream recycling bins that segregate recyclables and minimise cross-contamination at the source.

sections.label: 2019 Masterplan recycling targets
sections.summary: The 2019 Masterplan set a 70% recycling rate target by 2030 and a 30% cut in per capita daily landfill waste by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Under the 2019 Masterplan, we had set a target of 70% recycling rate by 2030 and to reduce the waste sent to landfill per capita per day by 30% by 2030.

sections.label: Dedicated paper and cardboard collection
sections.summary: NEA has worked with all PWCs to offer dedicated paper and cardboard collection in their zones since December 2025.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: To improve the quality and yield of paper and cardboard, NEA has also worked with all PWCs to offer dedicated collection of paper and cardboard in their respective zones since December 2025.

sections.label: Waste generation decline over decade
sections.summary: Domestic waste per capita fell 21% over the past decade, and non-domestic waste per unit GDP dropped over 30%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: Domestic waste generated per capita has fallen by 21% over the past decade, and non-domestic waste generated per unit gross domestic product has dropped by more than 30% over the same period.

sections.label: Industry partners and waste residue
sections.summary: It will work with industry partners to reduce risk and uncertainty of commercial use of waste residue and close resource loops.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: It will work with industry partners to reduce the risk and uncertainty of commercial use of waste residue and allow us to close our resource loops.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: We will engage the public and industry as part of the review process and share more details in due course.

sections.label: Waste generation per capita fall
sections.summary: Waste generation per capita fell from 1.06 kilogrammes in 2015 to 0.83 kilogrammes today, suggesting real progress lies upstream in waste prevention.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Our waste generation per capita has fallen from 1.06 kilogrammes in 2015 to 0.83 kilogrammes today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This suggests that Singaporeans are ready to try and reduce waste and also, then the real progress lies upstream in waste prevention.

sections.label: EU packaging and RFID suggestions
sections.summary: The suggestions on EU packaging regulations and possible RFID-based sorting of food waste can be looked at and considered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The suggestions that she has made around the EU's packaging regulations and potentially RFID-based sorting of food waste, these are all things that we can look at and we can consider.
